title: Our endangered world
subtitle: shrinking habitats, finite resources, sustainable development
summary: Use the standard collocations of environmental English - endangered species, carbon emissions, finite resources, sustainable development - to write and speak precisely about threats to the planet.

lesson.heading: Habitats and species under threat
lesson.text: **Shrinking habitats** - the places where animals live and breed are getting smaller - are a threat to **biodiversity**, the variety of biological species. **Endangered species**, types of plant or animal in danger of no longer existing, need legal protection if they are to survive.

examples.text: **Shrinking habitats** are a threat to **biodiversity**, in terms of both plants and animals.
**Endangered species** need legal protection if they are to survive.
These flowers are an **endangered species**, so it is illegal to pick them.

lesson.note: Habitat is countable; biodiversity is uncountable.

lesson.heading: Climate change and global warming
lesson.text: Although some **climate change sceptics** disagree, most scientists believe **global warming** - the steady rise in average world temperatures - will increase. This will make **polar ice** melt, resulting in **rising sea levels**. **Carbon (dioxide) emissions** from the burning of **fossil fuels** contribute to the **greenhouse effect**.

examples.text: **Climate change sceptics** do not believe that climate change is a serious issue.
Sea levels will rise if **global warming** continues.
**Carbon emissions** from cars and factories are a major problem.
Burning **fossil fuels** such as coal and oil causes a lot of pollution.

lesson.note: The greenhouse effect is the warming of the Earth's surface, where gases trap heat and redirect it back down.

lesson.heading: Pressure on resources
lesson.text: Population growth **exerts severe pressure on** (a formal way of saying puts great pressure on) **finite resources** - limited resources that will eventually run out. The **ecological balance**, the balance of natural relationships, may be upset by uncontrolled **deforestation**.

examples.text: Increasing population **exerts severe pressure on** economic resources.
We have to look after the **finite resources** of the planet.
If **deforestation** continues, there will be no forest left ten years from now.

lesson.heading: Projections and worst-case scenarios
lesson.text: **Demographic projections** - forecasts about the population - suggest the world population will continue to grow **exponentially**, that is extremely rapidly, putting extra pressure on **depleting resources**. One of the **worst-case scenarios** is that there will be no tropical rainforests left by 2050.

examples.text: **Demographic projections** suggest the world population will continue to grow **exponentially**.
Extra pressure is being put on **depleting resources**.
The **worst-case scenario** is a world choked by overpopulation and traffic gridlock.

lesson.heading: Waste, water and untouched places
lesson.text: **Waste disposal** - getting rid of waste - is an increasing problem, and **toxic waste** is **contaminating** many rivers and seas. Safe water may become a **precious commodity**, leading to issues of **water security**. Our hope is that **pristine environments** such as Antarctica can be preserved.

examples.text: **Toxic waste** is **contaminating** many rivers and seas.
Safe water is becoming an increasingly **precious commodity**.
A lot of Patagonia is a **pristine environment**, perfectly clean and untouched.

lesson.note: Water security is the ability to ensure that a population has safe drinking water.

lesson.heading: Phrases from the headlines
rows: a reputation for positive support of the environment, and policies that reflect this
people who always make the most pessimistic predictions about the future
development of industry which does not damage the environment and can continue over time
energy produced using sun, wind or crops rather than fuels which cannot be replaced

lesson.text: People cause damage to the environment, not ~~damages~~ - damage is uncountable here.

exercises.prompt: Match the words on the left with the words on the right to make environmental collocations.
These flowers are an endangered ___, so it is illegal to pick them.
exercises.hint: (a type of plant or animal in danger)
exercises.explanation: An endangered species is a type of plant or animal in danger of no longer existing.

exercises.prompt: A lot of wild animals have to survive in ___ habitats.
exercises.explanation: Shrinking habitats are places where animals live and breed which are decreasing in size.

exercises.prompt: A lot of Patagonia is a ___ environment that has never been touched.
exercises.explanation: A pristine environment is a perfectly clean, untouched, unspoilt area.

exercises.prompt: We have to look after the ___ resources of the planet because they will not last for ever.
exercises.explanation: Finite resources are limited resources that will eventually run out.

exercises.prompt: If ___ continues, there will be no forest left ten years from now.
exercises.explanation: Deforestation is the unrestricted destruction or clearing of forests.

exercises.prompt: Burning ___ fuels such as coal and oil causes a lot of pollution.
exercises.explanation: Coal, oil and similar fuels are fossil fuels.

exercises.prompt: Increasing population ___ severe pressure on economic resources.
exercises.explanation: To exert severe pressure on something is the formal way of saying to put great pressure on it.

exercises.prompt: Which correction is right? 'Unless we adopt a policy of ~~attainable~~ development, we will damage the planet.'
exercises.explanation: Sustainable development does not damage the environment and can continue over a period of time.

exercises.prompt: Which correction is right? 'Politicians are always trying to improve their green ~~potentials~~ in the eyes of the voters.'
exercises.explanation: Green credentials are a reputation for supporting the environment, backed by policy.

exercises.statement: Traffic and factories cause a lot of damages to the environment.
exercises.explanation: Damage is uncountable here: Traffic and factories cause a lot of damage to the environment.

exercises.statement: Prophets of doom and gloom always make the most pessimistic predictions about the future.
exercises.explanation: Correct - the phrase is prophets of doom and gloom, not profits.

exercises.prompt: Is each item a threat to the environment or a positive response to environmental problems?
Put this sentence about population in order.
exercises.answer: Demographic projections suggest the world population will grow exponentially
exercises.explanation: Demographic projections are forecasts about the population; to grow exponentially is to grow extremely rapidly.
